newsitem.title: UK: Moorfield details Greycoat merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Moorfield details Greycoat merger plan.

text.p: British property company Moorfield Estates Plc on Monday detailed its proposals for merging with its larger rival Greycoat Plc, which later this week faces a crucial vote on a shareholder rebellion aimed at breaking it up.
Moorfield said in a statement it had developed a proposal "to add value for all shareholders through a strategy of more active management of the assets of Greycoat".

This had been put to some of Greycoat's larger shareholders, accounting for a total of 40 percent of the group's shares. These shareholders had encouraged it to approach Greycoat's chairman and ask for detailed discussions.
Earlier Greycoat said the proposal was "vague as to value" and contained no new ideas. It said it did not propose to take the discussions with Moorfield any further "at this stage".

Moorfield's plan is to merge the two companies by the exchange of shares, valuing both at current net asset value "as established by external professional revaluations". Moorfield said a cash alternative held "no relevance for the Greycoat shareholders consulted so far".
The plan includes demerging the combined group's Central London portfolio, which would initially be made up of Greycoat's main assets, Embankment Place and 123 Buckingham Palace Road.

A portfolio of investment and development property would be earmarked for "immediate disposal to a major property company" and the remainder of the group's assets would form "an investment, trading and development portfolio".
There would also be a reorganisation of the board and management structure of the enlarged group to reduce corporate costs by at least 1.5 million stg a year.

Moorfield said the demerger of the Central London portfolio could provide "a basis for securitisation at the appropriate time". It said the enlarged core portfolio would be managed in accordance with its current strategy.
Greycoat's shareholders are due to vote on Thursday on a proposal by the UK Active Value Fund to sell-off mature properties.
Active Value Advisers, which advises the Active Value Fund, said in a separate statement it was "dismayed" by Greycoat's rejection of the Moorfield approach.

Brian Myerson, the South African financier behind the resolution to to break up Greycoat, said the company had "a duty to meet Moorfield and to put the detailed proposals before all shareholders so that they can decide on an informed basis".
Myerson also called for all shareholders to attend the meeting on Thursday and to vote in favour of his resolution.
